_comment: Artifact manifest for the canonical inference engine. Written by ops/manifests/regenerate.sh.
THE ENGINE IS A TREE, NOT A FILE. The launcher is 17,952 bytes and links 23 shared objects
beside it; a manifest naming only its hash cannot restore a working runtime. So this records
the whole directory -- every file with its own sha256, every symlink with its target -- and
names the bundle in the local release store that carries the bytes.
GIT CANNOT REBUILD THIS ARTIFACT AND THIS FILE DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. engines/ is
gitignored, the engine source carries no commit identity, and Handshake 4.2 recorded
STOP -- NOT REPRODUCIBLE after building it twice from one verified snapshot. The bundle is
the artifact of record BECAUSE it cannot be rebuilt. `bundle_sha256` is reproducible;
`source_reproducible` is false, and those are different claims.
Custody follows the archives/ convention already used for the DispatchOS preview archives:
a gitignored local release store holding <name>-<short>.tar.gz beside a key=value
MANIFEST.txt. This JSON is the half that lives in Git and points at it.

server.name: symoneural-llm
server.serving_proof: Handshake #108 phase 2 -- /proc/43122/exe hashed to this value while serving

cli.name: symoneural-llm-cli
cli.skew_note: bounded accepted skew; see ops/registry/SERVING-PATH.md. No matching CLI could be built.

custody.not_custody: the Handshake 1A rollback tree is audit evidence and is NOT a release store

_comment: WHERE the bundle can be obtained. Not what makes it acceptable.
This block is transport. `custody.bundle_sha256` above is the acceptance criterion,
and it is checked against the DOWNLOADED bytes -- a consumer resolves
manifest identity -> release artifact -> sha256 verification -> restore
and never 'GitHub says this is the right binary'. If a download and this manifest
disagree, the manifest is right and the download is rejected. Keeping it that way
round is what lets custody be replaced without renegotiating identity.
The release is PUBLIC and deliberately so. A private one would work, but retrieving
it needs a GitHub credential provisioned onto the rebuilt machine, which moves half
of disaster recovery into a second custody problem. The bundle is compiled runtime
binaries; the protected artefacts named in ENGINEERING.md -- training/corpus.jsonl,
training/build_dataset.py and training/adapter/ -- are not in it, checked member by
member and by scanning the binaries for corpus text before publication.
NO CREDENTIAL BELONGS IN THIS BLOCK. Retrieval is anonymous HTTPS; that is the point.
The tag names the runtime identity, not a source version. This engine has no commit
identity and no build record -- `source_reproducible` is false above -- so a semantic
version would assert a provenance nobody can demonstrate.
distribution.immutable: one asset per tag; a corrected artifact gets a NEW tag naming its new hash and never replaces an existing one

custody.restore_note: `restore` below is the LOCAL convenience form and assumes archives/ is already populated. A rebuilt machine has no archives/ -- it fetches the bundle to wherever it likes -- so tooling must use `extract_into` with the path it actually downloaded to. Found by reconstructing from a fresh clone: the recorded command worked only on a machine that already had the artifact, which is the one machine that does not need it.

source_reproducible_note: Handshake 4.2: STOP -- NOT REPRODUCIBLE. No commit identity, no build record, no preserved configuration.
consumed_by: backend/api.py LLM_ENGINE (default path; no environment override is set)
